findings: globally transitive robust probabilistic-bisimulation quotients for labelled Markov chains are existing prior art
perturbation-aware approximate probabilistic bisimulation is existing prior art
Fatmi robust bisimilarity is a continuity-stable subset of exact probabilistic bisimilarity rather than a generic epsilon-closeness merge rule
epsilon-perturbed bisimulation defines an existential nearby-model repair relation rather than identifying the exact unknown true partition
the LMC results do not preserve named action identity or quantify over all interventions
finite-sample calibration from empirical uncertainty to the perturbation model is not supplied
full-consequence labels must be independent of target IDs parser slots simulator names semantic rewards and evaluator codebooks
perfect recovery of robust P would still not identify Q or denotation d
counterexamples: action marginalisation can make two states globally robustly bisimilar as an LMC even though named actions produce swapped physical consequences and the controlled B4 quotient separates them

two confidence-consistent point models can have different exact quotients while both admit a small perturbation to one bisimilar repaired model, so epsilon-perturbed merging is not exact partition identification
kernel-level robustness to unconstrained independent probability perturbations can separate states whose equality is structurally tied by the physical data-generating mechanism
semantic target labels in the initial state labelling make robust refinement preserve supplied ontology rather than discover it
decision_text: Global robust and perturbation-aware probabilistic-bisimulation quotients are existing prior art for labelled Markov chains, but the available results do not provide action-complete full-consequence MDP identification, finite-sample perturbation calibration, semantic-codebook independence, or language-target coupling.
